Subject: Data residency & per-customer retention options

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement checklist we need finer-grained controls for where customer data is stored and how long it is retained. A couple of asks from our security/compliance team: 

- Ability to assign a retention policy per customer (not just org-wide), with options down to 30 days and up to 7 years.
- Regional residency controls so we can pin a customer’s data to a specific geo-zone (US-East, EU-West, APAC).
- Programmatic delete hooks and export proofs (audit log entries) when data is purged.

We attached a short CSV listing the initial set of tenants we care about and a draft spec (retention_spec_draft_v2.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-tenant retention today and, if not, what the recommended timeline would be to get this in production? Also: any implications for encryption keys / KMS or egress?

Appreciate a short sync or a clear action plan we can show Legal.

— Sarah
Security Lead, Acme Analytics

Thanks for flagging — I skimmed the spec. Quick thoughts and proposed approach: 

1) Product surface: we should expose a ‘Retention Profile’ object with: name, retention_window_days, storage_zone_hint, kms_key_id (optional), legal_hold flag, and a unique policy_id. Profiles can be attached to tenants via API and Console.

2) Storage model: implement logical “retention buckets” backed by region-tagged storage. Initially we can support three zones (us, eu, apac) and map policy->bucket. Migration path: allow changing policy (with a background data relocation job or a warning that change won’t retroactively move already-stored content).

3) Auditability: create immutable delete events logged to the audit subsystem (actor email, policy_id, object_count, before/after sizes). Expose an export endpoint and a pre-signed download for legal review.

4) Encryption & KMS: support tenant KMS binding for newly written objects. For re-encryption we’d need a background job; recommend we scope that out as a follow-on.

5) UX/API: Console editor + API endpoints (CRUD on Retention Profiles, assign to tenant_id). We should include sensible defaults and a set of compliance presets.

6) Priority & phasing: MVP = API + Console for profiles, region-tagged buckets, delete audit events for new deletes, tenant KMS binding for new data. Phase 2 = migration tooling, re-encryption, and legal-hold retention overrides.

Can you and Karthik call out engineering-level risks and give a rough estimate (MVP in sprints)? I’ll draft a short one-pager for Acme and Legal once we have rough timing.

— Priyom
Senior PM, Redwood Inference

Nice breakdown — engineering comments below: 

- Storage/buckets: Region-tagged buckets are straightforward if we treat residency as a metadata property and route new writes accordingly. The hard parts are backfill/migration and ensuring low-latency reads when a customer is geo-pinned to a remote region. We should provide a read-routing policy (primary-only or failover with cross-region reads).

- KV/indexing: We’ll need a tenant-to-bucket mapping in the serving layer plus a background scanner for objects that no longer match policy for eventual movement/deletion. Expect ~3–4 sprints to build foundational mapping + API endpoints.

- Audit events: We already have an audit pipeline; adding immutable delete events and an export endpoint is low cost (~1 sprint). Need to define schema for events (policy_id, source_region, deleted_by, deletion_time, object_count).

- KMS: Supporting tenant-bound KMS at write-time is feasible in 2 sprints for new objects (key ID propagation + envelope encryption). Re-encrypting existing objects is heavy — estimate a dedicated migration pipeline and throttle controls (phase 2).

- Compliance tests & e2e: add an e2e suite that simulates retention policy expiry, legal holds, and recovery/export. Plan ~2 sprints for tests and automation.

Rough roadmap (assuming we can start next sprint):
- Sprints 1–2: API/Console CRUD + tenant->bucket mapping + audit events (MVP).
- Sprint 3: Tenant KMS binding for new writes + export endpoint polish.
- Sprint 4: Backfill/migration prototype + e2e compliance tests.

Risks: cross-region read latency, storage egress costs during migration, and legal-hold complexity (must never delete during hold).

I can turn this into a technical RFC + JIRA epics. If Sales wants an earlier commitment for Acme we can propose a staged contract: feature-gate tenant KMS post-availability SLA.

— Karthik
Director, Infra Engineering
